Engineering Manager, Platform Team — Northfield Cloud (Jan 2023 – Present)
• Lead a team of six backend engineers who own and operate Northfield Cloud's internal deployment platform, used by engineering teams across the company.
• Set the team's roadmap for migrating internal services onto the company's new Kubernetes platform, sequencing the work across quarters.
• Own the platform team's quarterly cloud infrastructure budget, balancing spend against roadmap commitments.
• Hired three engineers onto the team, designing and running the technical interview loop for each.
• Run the team's incident postmortem process for platform outages, driving each incident to a documented root cause and follow-up actions.
• Represent the platform team in quarterly planning with the infrastructure and security organisations.

Senior Software Engineer, Platform Team — Northfield Cloud (Jun 2021 – Jan 2023)
• Led the design of the internal deployment tool now used by other engineering teams across the company.
• Built and maintained on-call rotation tooling adopted by three engineering teams; proposed the team's move to a standard on-call tool, which was adopted.
• Mentored two junior engineers through their first year on the team.
• Cut onboarding time for engineers new to the platform by rewriting the setup documentation.

Software Engineer — Amberlake Systems (Aug 2019 – Jun 2021)
• Built internal tooling for provisioning developer environments, including diagnosing and fixing a recurring race condition in the environment-provisioning queue.
• Contributed to the backend services team supporting the company's billing system, integrated with a third-party payment processor.
• Helped decompose the team's monolith into several smaller services.
• Wrote integration tests for the notification service and presented the team's testing practices in an internal talk.
• Participated in the on-call rotation for internal tooling.

Junior Software Engineer — Ridgeline Analytics (Jul 2018 – Aug 2019)
• Built small data-processing scripts for the analytics team and wrote unit tests for a new API endpoint.
• Set up the team's first shared staging environment and fixed bugs in the internal reporting tool.

Skills & context
• Production experience in Python and TypeScript, across data-processing scripts, backend services and internal developer tooling.
• Backend and cloud infrastructure: internal deployment platforms, Kubernetes migration, developer environment provisioning, on-call and incident tooling — relevant to a cloud-connected fleet dashboard.
• People leadership and mentoring: managing six engineers, hiring, and mentoring junior engineers.
• Note: my production work to date has been in backend and platform engineering; I have not built or deployed computer vision or machine-learning models in production, and have no C++ or embedded deployment experience. I am applying on the strength of production debugging, Python, infrastructure and team leadership, and would be moving into perception work from that base.

job.raw_text:
Machine Learning Engineer - Perception
Solstice Vision Labs - Onsite (Toronto) preferred, remote considered for senior candidates

About us

Solstice Vision Labs builds computer vision systems for autonomous inspection robots
used in warehouses and light manufacturing. Our perception stack has to work on
real, messy hardware in the field, not just in a notebook.

The role

We're looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to join our Perception team. You'll work
across the full lifecycle of our vision models: collecting and labeling data, training,
and getting models running reliably on the robot's onboard compute. This is a
production-focused role - we care more about a model that runs correctly on the robot
than one that looks good on a benchmark.

Responsibilities

- Build and improve computer vision models used in production on our robots
- Work with our data annotation pipeline to decide what gets labeled next
- Get models running within the memory and latency limits of embedded hardware
- Debug production failures back to a root cause, whether that's data, model, or camera
- Collaborate with hardware engineers on camera placement and calibration

What you'll need

- Hands-on experience building and deploying computer vision models to a production
  system, not only research or coursework
- Strong Python skills; C++ experience is a plus for the embedded-deployment side
- Experience with PyTorch or a comparable deep learning framework
- Experience working with a data annotation or labeling pipeline
- Comfortable working within hardware constraints such as edge or embedded deployment

Nice to have

- Peer-reviewed publications or patents related to computer vision or robotics
- Experience mentoring junior scientists or engineers
- Prior robotics industry experience
- Experience helping set technical research direction for a team, not just executing it
- Familiarity with backend or cloud infrastructure, for teams that also ship a
  cloud-connected fleet dashboard

Compensation & benefits

Salary band posted per local pay transparency requirements, equity, health benefits,
and relocation assistance for candidates moving to Toronto. Solstice Vision Labs is
an equal opportunity employer.
